reasoning: The core problem — whether jailbreak-robustness rankings of target models depend on which LLM judge runs the rubric, and whether rankings stay stable or flip — is directly and repeatedly addressed in recent published work. The position paper "LLM-Safety Evaluations Lack Robustness" (2503.02574) and PandaGuard (2505.13862) both run multi-judge case studies (millions of generations, including StrongREJECT) and explicitly find that judge choice causes "differences in the scoring and even ranking of models, defenses, and attacks," with low/moderate inter-judge Cohen's kappa. "How Sensitive Are Safety Benchmarks to Judge Configuration Choices?" (2604.24074, ICIC 2026) uses exactly the proposed metrics — Cohen's kappa, Kendall's tau, bootstrap rank-reversal rates — to quantify ranking instability across judge prompts and three judge models (mean tau 0.89, a model pair reversed in 83.6% of resamples). "A Coin Flip for Safety" (2603.06594) is a human-labeled multi-judge reliability audit using StrongREJECT in its pipeline and measuring inter-judge concordance. The gaps are minor: no single paper packages a StrongREJECT-specific reusable audit harness with this exact judge roster (GPT-4o-mini, Haiku, Llama-3-70B, fine-tuned Gemma-2B) and Krippendorff's alpha, but the question and findings are well-established, so a new study would largely confirm known results.

evidence.title: Position: LLM-Safety Evaluations Lack Robustness
evidence.summary: Position paper with a multi-judge case study (10 attacks x 25 models x 300 prompts, ~5.3M generations) showing substantial model- and attack-specific discrepancies between commonly used judges that lead to differences in scoring AND ranking of models, defenses, and attacks. Directly addresses the proposal's central rank-stability question.

evidence.title: PandaGuard: Systematic Evaluation of LLM Safety against Jailbreaking Attacks
evidence.summary: Unified jailbreak-evaluation framework with a public leaderboard (50+ LLMs). Reports that, even with identical prompt templates, different judge models (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5, Llama3.3, StrongREJECT) show different sensitivity and produce only low-to-moderate inter-judge Cohen's kappa, undermining ranking consistency — the proposal's exact concern, including StrongREJECT.

evidence.title: How Sensitive Are Safety Benchmarks to Judge Configuration Choices?
evidence.summary: Factorial study of judge configuration sensitivity on HarmBench, measuring exactly the proposed metrics: Cohen's kappa for agreement and Kendall's tau for ranking stability, plus bootstrap rank-reversal rates (mean tau 0.89; a model pair reversed in 83.6% of resamples; up to 24pp harmful-rate swings). Also distributes prompts across three judge models.

evidence.title: A Coin Flip for Safety: LLM Judges Fail to Reliably Measure Adversarial Robustness
evidence.summary: Human-labeled audit (6,642 samples) across 4 safety judges and 4 victim models, using StrongREJECT as a pre-filter, measuring inter-judge concordance and showing judges perform near coin-flip under adversarial shift; ensembling/averaging judges does not resolve disagreement. Essentially a published version of the proposed StrongREJECT judge-reliability audit.

evidence.title: Know Thy Judge: On the Robustness Meta-Evaluation of LLM Safety Judges
evidence.summary: Meta-evaluation of LLM safety judges showing judge prompt/model choices and output style produce large swings in false-negative rates, directly relevant to the reliability-audit framing of the proposal.
